note:
Import record for “Pyn's Character Archive”, Pynstripe's Bloodstar project, read the way
/bloodstar reads one: worker/bloodstar.js parsed the almanac, assets/bloodstar.js did the
mapping, and the objects below are what those two produced. Game data (team, ability, night
positions, night reminders, reminder tokens, setup, special) comes from script.json; the prose
(flavour line, overview, examples, how to run, tips, attribution) from each character's almanac
page. Nothing was written that the source does not say. Notes:
- The project carries no jinxes, no synopsis page, no changelog and no logo. The whole of its
  overview page is the line “Background by Adrian Salazar!”, which is kept as a Credit box on
  the collection page rather than being filed under a heading it does not answer to.
- The background is the image the project's own stylesheet sets, copied to
  assets/collections/pyn-s-character-archive-bg.jpg — that is what the credit line is about.
- Bloodstar has no tags, and tags are the importer's judgement rather than the author's, so
  every page is untagged. Curata on the collection is what keeps them out of Partial.
- Bloodstar has no Loric team either, so Pynstripe put the word in three names. Mythos,
  Goddess and Shapeshifter are filed under this wiki's `loric` team and the “(Loric)” suffix
  is dropped from the stored name. Nothing else about them changed, and none of the three is
  an official character (the names Goddess and Shapeshifter are shared, the abilities are not).
- 13 of the names already belong to pages here (Forager, Postmaster, Stargazer, Pawnbroker,
  Birdwatcher, Countess, Phantom, Mariner, Curator, Mummy, Impresario, Siren, Shapeshifter),
  so those take a -pyn-s-character-archive identity in the wiki's existing duplicate style.
  The other 82 keep their plain slug. Every page's ADDRESS is nested under the collection
  either way, so the suffix is never what a reader sees.
- The Aficionado has no art in either file, so it is the one page that lands as a draft:
  a character needs an icon before it can be published.
- The night order the almanac prints (8 first-night entries, 19 other-night) belongs to a
  script, and a collection has nowhere to keep an arranged one. Each character still carries
  its own firstNight/otherNight from script.json. Those are the author's own script-local
  numbers (first nights 11-18, other nights 2-20), not positions on the official global scale.
- The pages are unowned (owner_id NULL), like the rest of the bulk-imported wiki, so nothing
  resolves the credit “Pynstripe” to an account and the creator page renders in place at
  /author?a=Pynstripe. An admin can hand the set to Pynstripe with one assign-owner click,
  which carries all 95 character pages with it.
- Pynstripe's creator symbol (♣︎) was already registered in assets/creators.js.

data.name: Forager
data.ability: You start knowing 3 players. The first 2 share a trait the 3rd does not possess.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Forager learns that one of three players is different.
summaryBullets: The Forager only learns the players, not what trait they share. The first 2 players named share the trait, whilst the 3rd does not have it.
The trait that the players share can be anything so long as that is relevant to the game.
Of the players the Forager learns only two can share the trait.
howToRun: During setup, mark 2 players with FITS IN token, and 1 player with the ODD ONE OUT token. The 2 players with FITS IN tokens must share a trait (such as alignment, ability type, sober status, etc.) that the 3rd player with the ODD ONE OUT token does not possess.
On the first night, wake up the Forager to learn the 2 player with the FITS IN tokens, the and ODD ONE OUT token, in that order. Do not say who is the odd one out.
examples: Haunted is the Forager. His players are Pyn, Alex and Imze, where Imze is the odd one out. This is because both Pyn and Alex are Legion, and Imze is the Seamstress.
data.quote: Mama and Papa say that if I go huntin' for mushrooms, I'll go find something cool! I love seeing the birds and fungi and sometimes I pick up leaves to show them! But they don't want to see them when they are screaming at each other... Mama says she loves me more than anything in this house, and Papa says how he loves me more than anything in the world... but why don't they wanna see my leaf? It's symmetrical... I like it...,

data.name: Old Salt
data.ability: You start knowing an in-play minion, and you cannot die whilst they are alive.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Old Salt knows a threat in the game and cannot die unless the minion they learned is also dead or out of play.
howToRun: On the first night, mark a minion with the 'Known' token, and mark the Old Salt with the 'Cannot Die' token.
Wake the Old Salt, to learn the minion character who is marked with the 'Known' token.
If the Old Salt the minion knows dies or becomes out of play, remove the 'Cannot Die' token from the Old Salt.
examples: The Old Salt wakes to learn the Siren. If the Siren dies or becomes the Demon, the Captain can die.
data.quote: Weeeeellll me lad, you e've 'erd of the storms of seven'y-two?
data.firstNightReminder: Wake the Old Salt, and show them an in-play minion character.

data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Ombromanie may replace a Minion or Demon on their death.
summaryBullets: The Ombromanie does not have to add in their learned Minion and Demon.
The Ombromanie may only add in 1 of their learned characters.
Minions cannot become Demons or vice versa due to the Ombromanie's ability.

data.creator: Pynstripe

data.creator: Pynstripe

data.creator: Pynstripe

data.name: Pawnbroker
data.ability: You start knowing a character of each type, at-least 1 is in play. Each night*, you learn if one was nominated yesterday. [+0 or +1 Outsider]
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Pawnbroker learns a character of each type, and if one is nominated.
howToRun: During setup, place at-least 1 of the Pawnbroker's LEARNED tokens onto a player. Only 1 player of each type may have the LEARNED token, and multiple may be placed.

On their first night, wake the Pawnbroker to learn a character of each type. LEARNED characters must be included in the info, and if a type does not have an associated LEARNED player, the Pawnbroker must learn an out-of-play character for that type.
During nominations, mark if any LEARNED players that were nominated using the NOMINATED token.
Each Night, not the first, wake the Pawnbroker. If any NOMINATED tokens have been placed, tell them a 'yes' and send the Pawnbroker to sleep. If not, tell them a no.
examples: The Pawnbroker learns the Headliner, Faith Healer, Impresario and Veirot. The Impresario is the only one in-play. Today, they were nominated by the Vaudevillian. Tonight, the Pawnbroker wakes and learns "yes".
data.quote: How much is the memory of your objects worth?
data.firstNightReminder: Wake the Pawnbroker and show 1 character of each type, atleast 1 of which is in-play.
data.otherNightReminder: Wake the Pawnbroker and nod your head if a character they learned was nominated, or shake your head if one wasn't.

data.name: Au-pair
data.ability: Each night, you learn 2 players: either the 1st neighbours a Minion or the 2nd neighbours a Demon.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Au-pair watches over players that neighbour evil, with the knowledge that they're always recieving some false intel.
summaryBullets: The order of players learned by the Au-pair matters, as the 1st references a Minion's neighbour and the 2nd references the Demon's neighbour.
The false info learned by the Au-pair does not remain the same every night, and can change.
The Au-pair can learn themself and Travellers.
examples: Ryan is the Au-pair, who learns Kasumi and Jacob. Kasumi neighbours Emily the Mastermind, but Jacob does not neighbour the Demon.
The following night, Ryan learns Caitlin and Kasumi. Caitlin doesn't neighbour a Minion, but Kasumi neighbours Yvette the Pukka.
Yvette poisons Ryan the following night, when he learns Emily and himself. Both of these are true, as Emily's neighbour other than Kasumi is Julianna the Godfather, and Ryan also neighbours Yvette.
data.quote: Children! I understand you're having fun but we must return to the manor! I can't have you running off into the woods and making dark pacts! Your father already did that, and he'd be very displeased if you followed the same path!

data.name: Dressmaker
data.ability: Each night, learn the character type of the previously learnt player's clockwise neighbor (skipping Travellers).
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Dressmaker can learn a chain of character types.
howToRun: During Setup, mark a player with the Dressmaker's CUSTOMER' token.

Each night, wake up the Dressmaker to learn the character type of the player who currently has the CUSTOMER token. After the Dressmaker has gone to sleep, move the CUSTOMER token to that player's clockwise neighbour.
examples: On the first night, the Dressmaker is woken up and learns 'Outsider', as the player with the 'Customer' token is the Drunk. The following night, they learn 'Townsfolk' as they have learned themselves.
tips: The Dressmaker ONLY learns the character type, not the player.
data.quote: I dream in taffeta and chiffon. In them, I wear my own dresses and visit a midnight ball in a glistening emerald, with bodice and ruffle. I meet a man there, and we dance through the night til I return to... this. Where all I am is some formless mannequin. Where the dresses no longer fit or flatter but... examine the faults instead. I do not have a glass slipper, as the glass was already stabbed into me. And all that's coming out is fluff and tacky rhinestones.

data.name: Naturalist
data.ability: On your 1st & 3rd nights, choose Outsider, Minion or Demon. Each night, learn a player of an unchosen type. [+0 to +1 Outsider]
data.creator: Pynstripe

data.name: Tobacconist
data.ability: Each night, choose 3 characters (not the Tobacconist, & only once a Demon): learn if exactly 1 is in play.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Tobacconist can find out if 1 of 3 characters is in-play each night.
summaryBullets: The Tobacconist cannot select themselves.
Only 1 Demon can be chosen each game.
The Tobacconist only receives a yes if exactly 1 character they choose is in play. If they choose 0, 2 or 3 in play characters they receive a no regardless.
howToRun: Each night, wake the Tobacconist to choose 3 characters. They may not choose the Tobacconist. If they choose a demon, place the DEMON USED token and do not allow them to choose the Tobacconist again in the future. If they chose exactly 1 in-play character, the Tobacconist learns a yes, otherwise they learn a no.
data.quote: This world is a harsh, harsh place. Some people just need a vice to take the edge off, and it's just a service I offer. I sometimes take a drag, just to null it all, just for a second.
data.firstNightReminder: Wake the Tobacconist to choose 3 on-script characters (not Tobacconist): they learn 'yes' if exactly 1 is in play, and a 'no' otherwise. If they guess a demon, place the 'Demon Used' token, and they may not guess one again.
data.otherNightReminder: Wake the Tobacconist to choose 3 on-script characters (not Tobacconist(: they learn 'yes' if exactly 1 is in play, and a 'no' otherwise. If they guess a demon, place the 'Demon Used' token, and they may not guess one again.

data.name: Fireprod
data.ability: Each night, choose a player. You may (once) choose to learn which chosen player is closest to the Demon.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Fireprod sees whose close to the Demon.
summaryBullets: The Fireprod wakes at night, but does not learn information at night.

The Fireprod may only learn information once due to their ability, and cannot do so if dead. Gaining their info in private is up to the Fireprod’s choice, and the Storyteller may not prompt the Fireprod to receive their info.
The Demon is 0 steps from the Demon, which thus cannot neighbour themself to be the name learned by the Fireprod unless they are the only one.
If the Fireprod is drunk or poisoned whilst when they choose a player, they are not considered ‘chosen’ for the Fireprod’s ability.
If 2 chosen players are Equidistant, the Storyteller only names 1.
howToRun: Each night, wake the Fireprod to choose a player. Mark the chosen player with a TENDED reminder token and send the Fireprod to sleep. If the Fireprod is drunk or poisoned, do not place the TENDED reminder token - however, do keep mind that if they use their ability today the chosen player is still a valid choice. Do not wake the Fireprod if they have the NO ABILITY token on them.

Once per game, during the day, the Fireprod may have a private conversation with the Storyteller to use their ability. If this occurs, place the NO ABILITY reminder token on the Fireprod, and tell them which of the players with TENDED reminder tokens on them sits closest to the Demon.
examples: Nycto is the Fireprod, who chooses Tom the Marionette and Ella the Chambermaid. On Day 2, Nycto visits the Storyteller and learns that Tom is the closest chosen player to the Demon.

Luis is the Drunk who believes he is the Fireprod. He chooses Dark the Beauty, Ice the Undertow and himself. On Day 3, Luis visits the Storyteller and incorrectly learns that Ice is the closest chosen player to the Demon.

It is a Lord of Typhon Game. Lady Mist the Poisoner poisons Sooth the Fireprod when he chooses her, and thus cannot be learned as the player closest to the Demon if he uses his ability (without choosing her again.)
data.quote: Oh it’s awfully chilly outside, please, I do ask that you stay in. I shall have the maids prepare some hot tea, we shall find you a novel that best fits your inclinations, and we shall stay close to the fireplace.
data.firstNightReminder: Wake the Fireprod to choose a player, they are marked with a 'Tended' reminder token.
data.otherNightReminder: If the Fireprod has used their 'Once per game' ability, do not wake them. Wake the Fireprod to choose a player, they are marked with a 'Tended' reminder token.

data.name: Birdwatcher
data.ability: Each night*, if you did not nominate yesterday, you learn how many Townsfolk did.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Birdwatcher learns how many Townsfolk nominated yesterday, if they didn’t.
summaryBullets: If the Birdwatcher nominates, they do not wake tonight. This does not include the Birdwatcher attempting to exile a traveller.
The Birdwatcher learns how many Townsfolk nominated. If an Outsider, Minion, Demon or Traveller nominate, the total does not increase.
The Birdwatcher still learns about evil Townsfolk.
The Birdwatcher’s number is true for the day, instead of the night: if a Townsfolk nominated, then changed character during the night, the Birdwatcher’s number doesn’t decrease.
data.quote: Stay perfectly still…. you don’t want to alert…. the rare and elusive… greenfinch….

data.name: Caroller
data.ability: Each night*, learn a Townsfolk that claimed to be a Caroller today, if you did & another Caroller or Demon didn’t. [+0 to +1 Caroller]
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Carollers want other players to join in their song.
summaryBullets: There can be up to 2 Carollers in the bag, but there doesn't have to.

Each day, players may "sing". This is a claim, similar to the Gossip, Alsaahir, or the 'I Am Spartacus!' mechanic from the popular homebrew script Fall of Rome. When "singing", players don't literally have to sing, but may do so if they wish.
Starting on the 2nd night, if 1 Caroller "sang" they learn a Townsfolk who sang as well. If multiple Carollers or the Demon "sang" too, no Carollers wake.
Drunk or Poisoned Carollers can wake if they shouldn't or vice versa.
data.quote: Tis’ the non-denominational winter festival season to be jolly! Fa-La-La-La La! La-La-La-L- What do you mean it’s October? It’s non-denominational winter festival season in my heart…

data.name: Eulogist
data.ability: Each night*, you learn which player that died since dawn helped your team the most.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Eulogist compares how useful dead players are.
summaryBullets: If no player was executed, or no player died tonight, the Eulogist does not wake.
data.quote: She was always so funny, kind, generous with her time, and courageous in the face of danger. He was also here. Not anymore though!

data.name: Headliner
data.ability: Each night*, you are drunk if evil was executed yesterday, & learn how many other nominees would have been a good execution for you.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Headliner learns whose execution may benefit them.
summaryBullets: The Headliner learns specifically information as it relates to themself, not their team. If the Headliner believes a good nominee is the demon, you may add it to their number to disprove it upon execution.
If any evil player (not just Minions or Demons) is executed, the Headliner is drunk until they next wake.
The executed player may not count towards the Headliner’s number.
data.quote: The peroxide lingers, as all the rumours buzz around like bees to my beehive. I’m a literal bigwig. Look at my scowl. It’s mean, yet seductive, yet repulsed, who could want more?

data.ability: Each night*, choose 3 characters of different types: if only 1 is in-play, they die (if good), or you die (if evil).
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Optician kills those clear in their sights, but if they're evil, dies in their stead.
data.quote: No no, I have perfect vision. Why else would I become an Optician! Sometimes I drop things, that's normal! That's called having perfect 5/5 star vision. Now where did I leave the chart of various smudges...

data.name: Burglar
data.ability: Each night*, the Demon chooses a unique player: you learn them & their character. If you, you learn this & lose your ability.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.quote: ’Old it, ‘old it! Whaddaya sayin’, we stole a fake idol? But it’s all… shiny! That’s gotta be worth… summin!

data.name: Vaudevillian
data.ability: Each night*, learn if you voted for a Minion yesterday. If you nominated, learn if you voted for the Demon instead.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Vaudevillian learns if they voted for a Minion yesterday, or more powerful information if they also nominated.
data.quote: Chicken feathers?! I am appalled by such a fowl accusation! This is authentic peacock!

data.name: Aficionado
data.ability: Each day, even if dead, choose a player & learn a fact about them. It’s true whilst you live & false if you die, or vice versa.
data.creator: Pynstripe

data.name: Bankshot
data.ability: Each day, you may visit the Storyteller to learn a question with a unique numerical answer.
data.creator: Pynstripe

data.name: Lace Runner
data.ability: There is a pattern to the bluffs. Each day, you may privately learn a statement about the bluffs.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Lace Runner defines a pattern amongst the bluffs.
summaryBullets: Amongst the bluffs, the Storyteller must define a pattern. It may be complex or simple, but there must be a quantifiable thread which links all the bluffs together.
Each day, the Lace Runner may privately learn a fact about the bluffs, which may concern specific characters or the pattern.
examples: The bluffs are Undertaker, Monk & Ravenkeeper. They are a pattern as they are consecutive characters on the script sheet. During the day, the Lace Runner learns that 2 of the bluffs share a waking pattern.
data.quote: Oi, Matilda! Stop pokin' me! You'll make me spill red juice all over this fine cloth, then I won't earn my penny for my hard weeks work!

data.name: Lady-in-Waiting
data.ability: Each day, you may privately learn something the opposing team should not.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Lady-in-Waiting has scandalous rumours.
summaryBullets: The Lady-In-Waiting learns true statements that the evil team would benefit to know.
It is up to the Lady-in-Waiting to talk with the Storyteller, not the other way around. This isn’t a public conversation, and the group can’t listen in. It’s private.
The Lady-in-Waiting can choose to not visit the Storyteller if they wish.
examples: Nima is the Lady-in-Waiting. She privately learns that the Magician neighbours a Minion. Kiki the Magician neighbours Hector the Scarlet Woman.
data.quote: The ritual of bathing has many luxuries: tiny French pastries, rose bath salts, a notebook detailing the mistress’ scandalous pastimes, and where the press will be so we can rendezvous.

data.name: Quarryman
data.ability: Each day, privately name a simple event to the Storyteller & learn how likely it is to occur. If impossible, you learn false information.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Quarryman can learn the likelihood something happens, but can never learn of impossibilities.
summaryBullets: A response to the Quarryman should take the form of a word, like “Certain” and “Unlikely”.
If the Quarryman asks for the likelihood for an event that is impossible to predict, ask them to ask for a new statement.
It is not up to the Storyteller to seek out the Quarryman, it is the other way around.
The Quarryman must say their event in private.
howToRun: Each day the Quarryman may have a private conversation with the Storyteller and say an event that could happen in the game, and the storyteller must respond with a probability, like "Unlikely", "Certain" or "Very Likely".
If it is impossible to predict, ask them to state a new question. If the event itself is impossible, the Storyteller must lie to the Quarryman, giving a different possibility.
data.quote: Why is it fair that some people strike gold and win big, whilst others, and others are stuck searching for their entire lives. I sometimes wonder if this was ever worth it. There ain't no gold in my mines, it seems. Only slate.

data.name: Salesman
data.ability: Once per game, at night, choose a player: learn another whose closest evil neighbour is the same number of steps from them.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Salesman learns 2 players who equally close to evil.
summaryBullets: The direction of the neighbours doesn't matter, just the step count.
The Salesman must learn about neighbours, even if the chosen player is evil.
If no other players are the same number of steps away from a chosen evil, the Salesman learns a no.
examples: Neil is the Salesman, who chooses himself. Neil's closest evil neighbour is Izzy the Xaan who is 2 steps away. Neil then learns Taha the Butler, whose closest evil neighbour, Eva the Recluse (registering as evil), is also 2 steps away.
data.quote: It’s such a pain visiting every city in the country in a single trip without revisiting any of them! And I have to calculate the most efficient way?! What does a man have to do to get a simple job?!

data.name: Countess
data.ability: Once per game, at night*, you may choose to learn who the Demon is. If the Demon nominates, you learn false info until dusk.
data.creator: Pynstripe

data.name: Chanteuse
data.ability: If the Demon just killed the most important good player, you are woken to learn an evil player.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Chanteuse gets payback for killed good players.
summaryBullets: The most important good player is a subjective assessment, and can be based on many factors, such as that players’ ability or what that player believes about the game.
The player learned must be killed by a Demon attack. Being executed does not count.
If the Chanteuse is the most important good player and is killed by the Demon, they do not wake to learn an evil player, because they are dead.
howToRun: If the player you believe to be the most important good player died tonight, wake the Chanteuse. Point at any evil player. Put the Chanteuse to sleep.
examples: The Demon kills the Poppy Grower, the most important good player. That night, the Chanteuse wakes and learns the False Prophet.
There is a Rattlefog in-play. The Chanteuse nominated yesterday. The Demon kills the Apparition, who is not the most important good player, but the Chanteuse wakes and learns the Investigator.
tips: It is possible for multiple players to be the “most important good player”, such as how almost all good players are “most important” if a Legion is in-play, as there are very few good players alive.
data.quote: Draped in finery and host to the heavenly call of a principality's vocal range, I've sung for kings, barons, cardinals and contessas. I'm like a moth, drawn to organ song and chorus accompaniment. Mesmerised, darling - I'm sure.
data.otherNightReminder: If the player you believe to be the most important good player died tonight, wake the Chanteuse. Point at any evil player. Put the Chanteuse to sleep.

data.name: Phantom
data.ability: On the final night, learn you are a Phantom, even if dead. [Phantoms think they're different bluffs. +0 to +2 Phantoms]
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Phantoms hide in what the Demon thinks is safe.
summaryBullets: There may be multiple Phantoms, & if so, each much think they are a different bluff.
Any bluff learned is a valid option for a Phantom to think they are, including bluffs learned by the Summoner or if the Snitch provides Minions bluffs.
If there are less learned bluffs than Phantoms, some Phantoms may think they’re the same bluff.
examples: The Demon’s bluffs are Dreamer, Innkeeper & Mayor. There are 2 Phantoms, who think they are the Dreamer & Innkeeper respectively. When the Phantom who thinks they are the Innkeeper dies, they learn this tonight.

There are 3 Phantoms, who each think they're the Clockmaker, Chambermaid & Flowergirl respectively. However, the Phantom who believes they're the Flowergirl neighbours the No Dashii. As the Phantoms thinking they're bluffs is setup text, the Phantom becomes drunk & keeps thinking they're a bluff. On the final night, they do not learn they're a Phantom.
The Amnesiac’s ability is “The Demon only learns 1 bluff”. That bluff is the General. There are 3 Phantoms, all of whom believe they are the General as it’s the only bluff.
data.quote: Do you hear the wailing of the lonely soul, bound by salt diagrams & thrust into the most tortuous midnight? It is I, the most tormented soul in this castle - no ghoul could ever match my pitiful existence, for it is a solitary torture.

data.name: Conservationist
data.ability: If one of your living neighbours is the Demon & another evil player lives, they swap characters. When you die, learn if this happened.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Conservationist prevents the Demon from disturbing the natural world.
summaryBullets: The Demon may swap to any of living evil players, so long as they are living & don’t neighbour the Conservationist.,
The Demon may swap characters with evil Minions, Outsiders and Townsfolk. The Demon may not swap characters with a Traveller.,
If the only living evil players are both the living neighbours of the Conservationist, no change happens.
data.quote: This is our locus amoenus, we must seek to conserve it’s edenesque imag- No, it’s not locust. And no, it’s actually quite nice, not mean in the slightest. I should have just said it’s a nice place. That would have gotten the message across easier.

data.name: Laureate
data.ability: On the final night, choose & gain an approved off-script “Once per game” ability. If you’re dead, the Storyteller chooses for you.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Laureate gains inspiration from unforeseen spaces.
summaryBullets: The Laureate may only gain off script abilities. This does include homebrew, so long as your players understand which may enter play & their abilities.
The Laureate may gain abilities of any type.

The Storyteller must approve the Laureate's choice of ability. The Laureate may ask in advance if certain abilities would be allowed or not, and the Storyteller has final say over the potential abilities.
howToRun: On the final night, if the Laureate lives, show them the approved "Once per game" characters tokens, and they choose 1 to gain the ability of. If the Laureate is dead, choose for them.
Run the chosen (or given) ability as per usual, even if the Laureate is dead. I
examples: Noah is the living Laureate, who chooses to gain the Artist’s ability. The following day, he asks if Lara the Legislator is the Demon, and learns a no.

Abdallah is the dead Laureate, who gets given the Courtier’s ability by the Storyteller. He chooses to make the Cerenovus drunk. Nothing happens when Lars the Cerenovus attempts to make Abdallah mad about being the Mutant.
data.quote: In the poem "Harromog and Modos", I analysed the skeletons one has in their closet. Not mine, I have no secrets. No love affairs either, for you see I'm... just a bachelor. I had that confirmed when I consulted the dic-tionary. Also I ask you to stop analysing my particularly named mineral collection, my Adamite, Marcasite and Fergusonite have nothing to do with any of this.
data.otherNightReminder: On the final night, wake the Laureate and show them the "Once per game" characters to choose from - they choose 1, which they gain the ability of. If the Laureate is dead, choose for them, then show the Laureate the chosen token.

data.name: Mariner
data.ability: Your Townsfolk neighbours must learn true info. If you're mad about being the Mariner, you become a different Townsfolk tonight.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Mariner can sink or swim.
summaryBullets: If the Mariner has not claimed to be the Mariner, their Townsfolk neighbours must learn true information, even if drunk, poisoned, or subjected to reversed / false information.
If the Mariner claims to be the Mariner, they become a different Townsfolk the following night, losing this ability.
The Mariner can become in-play Townsfolk or bluffs.
The Mariner's Townsfolk neighbours remain consistent, even if those neighbours die.
If the Mariner changes character, they may not change back.
examples: Rhea is the Mariner, whose Townsfolk neighbours are Wyatt the Knight & Li the Ravenkeeper. It is a Vortox game. Wyatt correctly learns Cath & Li are not the Demon. When Li dies, she chooses Rhea & learns she is the Mariner.
James is the Mariner. He is mad about being the Mariner, & becomes the Artist tonight. His Townsfolk neighbours no longer learn true info.
data.quote: Seas are calm tonight. Well, calm compared to the port at least. Port? Did someone say wine?

data.name: Muse
data.ability: Your most recent nominee is sober, healthy & learns true info. If they’re alive & evil, you might learn this at night.
data.creator: Pynstripe

data.name: Reverend

data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Reverend can help a Minion repent and win with good.
data.quote: The light shall cleanse you.

data.name: Well-Wisher
data.ability: Wishes made by the 1st player executed might come true.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Well-Wisher can make the wishes of the 1st executed player come true.
summaryBullets: Wishes made by the 1st executed player might come true. Which wishes come true or not is dependent on the Storyteller.
Depending on the strength of the wishes, the Storyteller should make 1 wish come true each day. If stronger wishes are made, the Storyteller may make them happen once in total.
The Well-Wisher only makes the wishes of the 1st player executed come true, not any other player. If the Well-Wisher dies, future wishes cannot come true.
data.quote: Those stars sure are pretty...

data.name: Apparition
data.ability: You think you're a Townsfolk. Players you nominate become the Apparition instead of you. If they're the Demon, the Storyteller now is.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Apparition possesses different players, and potentially, makes town need to execute the Storyteller to win.
howToRun: Like the Drunk or Marionette, do not place the Apparition's token into the bag. Replace it with an additional Townsfolk token. During Setup, place the global 'Is the Apparition' token on a Townsfolk.
During the day, if the player with the 'Is the Apparition' token nominates, move the 'Is the Apparition' token to the player they nominated.

If the Demon has the 'Is the Apparition' token on them, the Storyteller now needs to be executed for good to win, until the Demon nominates again. Thus, allow nominations and executions of the Storyteller even if the Apparition is not in play.
If the Demon is not the Apparition and the Storyteller is executed, good loses. If the Demon is the Apparition and the Storyteller is executed, good wins.
examples: The Apparition believes they are the Electrician. They nominate the Ruffian. The Starting Apparition is now the Electrician, and the starting Ruffian is now the Apparition.
The Apparition nominates the Hush. The starting Hush's ability malfunctions and good needs to execute the Storyteller, as the Hush is now the Apparition, until the starting Hush nominates.
tips: If you believe you are the Apparition, it is better to nominate players you believe to be minions rather than players you think are the Demon, to prevent the Storyteller needing to be executed and Minions gain no benefit from being the Apparition.
data.quote: *ominous water noises*

data.name: Beauty
data.ability: The 1st evil executee doesn’t die (& you can't die until then).
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Beauty makes the first evil player executed survive, and they cannot be executed until an evil player has been.
howToRun: During the day, if an evil player has been executed for the first time, they do not die, and the Beauty's 'Can Die' token is placed on the Beauty.
examples: The Wicked is executed on Day 1, and doesn't die due to the Beauty's ability. Now, if the Beauty is executed, they die.
tips: Keep silent about being an Outsider, but try to get executed covertly during the day. Your survival or death to an execution speaks volumes, and can reveal if an evil player has been executed yet.
data.quote: In life and death, Beauty is forever. May my grace and poise inspire you through hardship.

data.name: Bedfellow

data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Bedfellow’s dying wish is that others keep their secret.
data.quote: We take our secrets - both big and small - with us to the grave. Don't tell anyone how you truly knew me, there'll be so many at the funeral that my family will be bound to ask questions.

data.name: Bellboy

data.creator: Pynstripe

data.quote: MA'AM PLEASE SLOW DOWN THESE BAGS ARE... H-HEAVY... WHY ARE THEY FULL OF BRICKS OH GOD

data.name: Cardmaker
data.ability: If you die, Minions have their abilities whilst dead.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Cardmaker needs to live, to prevent evil from keeping their own abilities in death.
howToRun: If a Minion dies, check if the Cardmaker is dead. If they are alive, do nothing. If they are, place the Cardmaker's HAS ABILITY token on that dead Minion. If the Cardmaker dies, mark all dead evil players with the HAS ABILITY token.
If it's a dead Minion's turn in the night order and they have the HAS ABILITY token on them, wake them to perform their night action.
data.quote: Don't worry about the pattern, it's supposed to be that way.

data.name: Composer
data.ability: After day 9, evil wins: each time a good player is executed, the end comes 2 days sooner (even if dead).
data.creator: Pynstripe

data.name: Curator
data.ability: You start knowing a question. If you die, you must correctly answer it tomorrow (once) or your team loses.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.quote: I once wished to be a dinosaur. Those dreams were squashed as I placed their bones in see through cases. How free they were, how relentless - now only that harsh, bone-like truth remains.

data.name: Endling
data.ability: You are the only unique good character. The bluffs are in-play good characters. [Other good characters are duplicates. Odd Outsider Count]
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Endling is the last of their species, and therefore unique.
summaryBullets: For other good characters, more than 1 may be in play. For evil characters, exactly 1 of each have to be in play.
The Endling modifies setup so there’s an odd number of Outsiders. This can reduce the number of Outsiders in play. This is because setup would become impossible if exactly 2 Outsiders are in play.
Only good characters are duplicated due to the Endling's ability. Evil characters, Fabled and Travellers are unaffected.
Any learned bluffs are in-play characters. This includes bluffs that are not learned by the Demon.
data.quote: Hello there. My name is Martha. What’s yours?

data.name: Faith Healer
data.ability: You start knowing the Demon character. Good players mad it’s in play might die at any time, even if dead.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Faith Healer knows it’s enemy, but causes harm if it’s discussed.
summaryBullets: The Faith Healer know the Demon's character, the one of the (usually) four Demons listed at the bottom of the script that is in play. If multiple of these are in play, the Faith Healer only learns one.
If a good player is mad the in-play Demon is in-play, they might die at any time, during either the day or at night. The Faith Healer can die to their own ability,
If the Demon's character changes, the Faith Healer still punishes those who discuss the initial type.
howToRun: During the first night, wake the Faith Healer to learn the Demon's character. Put them to sleep.

If a good player is mad about the in-play Demon's character being in-play, place one of the Faith Healer's MIGHT DIE token on them. They might die at any time. Only 5 are included, and if this is not enough, use custom tokens or a note. You may continue to add MIGHT DIE tokens even if the Faith Healer is dead, but not drunk or poisoned.
data.quote: My dearest child, close your eyes and scream to free all those demons held within your brain. Release those ailments and malignancies, and let out the hatred whilst I touch my head to your forehead. Please, release those innocent juvenile tears my dearest of god's flock. They're screams of joy and happiness, tears of salvation... and I move onto the next. My dearest child...

data.name: Fog Rover
data.ability: Evil players might register as good Fog Rovers. Once per game, at night, learn if the Demon has done so since dawn.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Fog Rover hides evil players as itself, but can find the Demon in its haze.
summaryBullets: All evil players, even if they are not Minions or Demons, may register as good Fog Rovers. They may continue to register as evil and their character (and the Demon is still "the Demon" for the purposes of winning or losing), but this is up to Storyteller discretion.
The Fog Rover's misregistration only occurs whilst the Fog Rover lives. The Fog Rover may not use their ability if they are dead.
The Fog Rover's misregistration continues if they use their ability
examples: Imze is the evil Reverist, but as the Fog Rover is in play and alive he might register as a good Fog Rover. De is the Dressmaker who learns an Outsider on Imze due to the Fog Rover's ability, even though the Dressmaker's 'Customer' token normally can not be placed onTravellers.
data.quote: Hide in the fog with me.... the world can't hurt you now...

data.name: Fraud
data.ability: You have an in-play Townsfolk’s ability. Each night, until correct, the Demon guesses which: if correct, you turn evil & keep your ability if dead.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Fraud may sell out to evil.
summaryBullets: The Fraud learns an in-play Townsfolk ability, and has it whilst they live. The Fraud cannot learn about an ability which is thought to be in play but is actually a character like the Drunk.

Each night, the Demon chooses a Townsfolk ability. If the Fraud has that ability, they become evil and keep their ability whilst dead. The Demon does not learn that they have made the Fraud evil, but they stop waking on subsequent nights to guess the Fraud's Townsfolk ability.
If the Fraud is good and dies, they do not keep their ability whilst dead, and the Demon stops guessing their character at night.
examples: Luis is the Fraud who also has the Tobacconist's ability. On the first night, he learns that only 1 of the Pawnbroker, Oracle and Bellboy are in-play.

Ella is the Fraud who has the Vaudevillian's ability. Both Ella and Amelia, who is actually the Vaudevillian, use their abilities on the same day. The following night, the Demon guesses the Fraud has the Vaudevillian's ability, and Ella turns evil.
data.quote: I want her everything. Her style. Her eyes. The Marilyn of it all.

data.name: Mummy
data.ability: If you die, the Demon may gain up to 3 non-Demon abilities tonight until dusk. If they only gain 1 & it's good, they keep it.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Mummy either thaws quickly or is long preserved.
data.quote: Not all of us wear bandages. Some of us wear scars. And tears. And tales. And it's all over us.

data.name: Summer Fling
data.ability: You start knowing an in-play Minion. If an ally is executed, you swap alignments tonight & if evil, have the learned Minion ability.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.quote: I can do even more with 15 minutes - trust me. Meet me at dawn and you'll then search for me ‘til the deep dusks of winter, but you'll never be anything more to me. Never.

data.name: Angolde
data.ability: Each night*, you may choose a player: they die. Each day, if a player you killed guesses you (once), you die.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Angolde can kill easily, yet dies if it’s correctly guessed.
summaryBullets: The killed player needs to guess who the Angolde is, and each player may only guess who Angolde is once each day.
Nothing happens if an incorrect guess is made.
Players killed on previous days may still guess they were killed by the Angolde.
howToRun: Each day, players may guess who the Angolde is. If a player with the DIVINE token correctly guesses who the Angolde is, immediately announce that they have died, marking them with their own DEAD token.

Each night, except the first, wake the Angolde and ask if they want to use their ability. If no, put them to sleep. If yes, they point at a player: they die, and are marked with the Angolde's DEAD and DIVINE tokens.
data.quote: Heaven’s gate was built for me, in it’s eternal glory - yet so quickly it was shut on my face. My many eyes flickered, my mouths screamed incomprehensibly. I swore revenge on those bastard seraphim and throne. I shall reclaim heaven, and it’s spoils will be MINE!
data.otherNightReminder: Wake the Angolde, they may either shake their head or point at a player, then put the Angolde to sleep. If they pointed at a player, mark them with the Angolde's Dead and Divine tokens.

data.name: Entity
data.ability: If you die, something good happens for the evil team & you learn it. Suggestions for what happens if you die might become true.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Entity is formed by what it’s feared to be.
summaryBullets: The Entity’s ability has no impact before they die. Once they die, one suggestion to what happens occurs.
If no player suggests what the Entity’s death will cause, the Storyteller decides & must use this to heavily help evil (without making them win).

Unless stipulated by the suggestion, what occurs on the Entity’s death is not stated (this includes if the Storyteller decides). If a suggestion stipulates an announcement, it must become much better for evil than a regular suggestion.
If the Entity dies at night, the Storyteller is allowed to choose / create a weaker impact to occur.
examples: Michael is the Entity. Viv the Shugenja who suggests that when the entity dies, all info learned by Townsfolk from now on will be false. Patrick the Zealot suggests that the only way to win from now on is via forming a cult. Michael dies by execution and grants him Viv’s suggestion, making all information false from now on.

Andre the Entity suggests that the Entity will see the Grimoire if they die. Eugene the Po suggests that the Entity will become a Cerenovus who uses their ability twice. Renée the Savant suggests that evil wins at dusk tomorrow. Eugene kills Andre in the night, and the Storyteller enacts the least damaging option, so Andre sees the Grimoire tonight.
data.quote: formless dreaming of an unexplainable forever shifting shape trying to fit into a limitless puzzle

data.name: Gizmo
data.ability: Once per game, at night, choose a Demon: become it, & if you don’t claim Gizmo when nominated you lose if executed.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Gizmo wildly changes evils lineup, but is very honest.
summaryBullets: The Gizmo does not have to claim to be it before using its once per game ability.
data.quote: Lets see what happens when I take this cog! Oopsie! I’m sorry Mr Clockwork, it seems like you won’t go tick tock anymore…

data.name: Grandiose
data.ability: You have every on-script “Once per Game” ability. If you die, choose 1 unused ability to keep (not this).
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Grandiose has every ability that can only be used once.
summaryBullets: If an ability contains the phrase “Once per Game”, the Grandiose may use it. They may only use it once, and do not gain access to other parts of their ability.
The Grandiose uses the abilities at their regular times. If they have the Courtier’s ability they use it at night. If they have the Fisherman’s ability they use it during the day.,

If the Grandiose dies, they choose 1 on script “Once per Game” ability that they have not used yet and may continue to use it. They may not choose abilities they’ve already used, and lose the abilities they did not choose, even if they were unused.,
The Grandiose doesn't have to use their abilities if they do not wish.
data.quote: In my manor of catastrophes, many will give their lives to overcome the challenges. Like moths to a gothic fireplace. They have 1 shot in this halls and yet they throw them away… shameful, they don’t see how only their powers combined can find their way to my sanctum.

data.name: Hired Gun
data.ability: Your most recent good nominee is poisoned & might register as you would, even if you were executed.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Hired Gun poisons & frames their most recent good nominee.
data.quote: I'd rather not know your name. It's not like it'd sway me, I sold my sympathies years ago. I just don't want to give you false hope.

data.name: Impresario
data.ability: Once per game, at night, choose to become the character executed tomorrow (unless 3 live). Each day, if no-one is executed, evil wins.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Impresario puts specific focus on a single day, yet demands performances on each.
summaryBullets: Evil wins if nobody is executed whilst the Impresario is untransformed. If the Impresario becomes a different character, evil does not win if nobody is executed.
The Impresario remains evil, regardless of which character is executed.
If the Demon is executed, the Impresario becomes the Demon before the game ends.
The Impresario cannot change character if only 3 live.
howToRun: Each night, wake the Impresario and ask if they want to use their ability. If no, send them to sleep. If yes, place the OPERA TODAY token onto the Impresario.

If a player is executed whilst the Impresario has the OPERA TODAY token on them, the Impresario becomes their character. For online play, change the Impresario's token and place the IMPRESARIO'S ABILITY token to indicate they are the Impresario. The Impresario becomes the character executed before the day ends, and cannot change character when 3 live.
Each day, if the Impresario has not changed characters and no player was executed, announce that the game is over and evil has won.
data.quote: Hit those upper operatic tones, Angelique! Raise the heavens! Do I need to put on a mask and chase you through the wings, become some sort of... Phantom of the Operetta? I wish not.
data.firstNightReminder: Wake the Impresario to choose a day.
data.otherNightReminder: If the Impresario's chosen day was yesterday, wake them to become the executed character.

data.name: Malady
data.ability: You start by seeing the Grimoire, choosing a player & an Outsider: they gain its ability, & another player thinks they do.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Malady ails a chosen player with an Outsider’s ability.
summaryBullets: The chosen player only gains the chosen Outsider's ability, does not become that Outsider. Thus, duplicate outsider abilities may be in play. If an Outsider on script would become evil, add a Spirit of Ivory.
The Malady can choose any player, even outsiders, minions or demons. A good player, must learn the Malady & it’s 2 chosen players.
The chosen player and a different player of the Storyteller's choice learn the Malady and the chosen Outsider.
The ability stops functioning when the Malady dies.
howToRun: On the 1st night, wake the Malady to view the Grimoire, and prompt them to choose a player & Outside character, before sending the Malady to sleep. Mark the chosen player with the AILED token, and mark a different player with the FAUX reminder token. Individually wake the players with the AILED and FAUX reminders (in any order) and point to the Outsider chosen by the Malady, before sending them to sleep.

Only the player with the AILED reminder token has the chosen Outsider ability, yet the player with the FAUX token thinks they do as well. If the Outsider would wake, both do, but only the AILED player has an impact on the game. It is recommended you write down the chosen outsider.
If the Malady would become drunk, poisoned, or die, remove the AILED and FAUX reminder tokens.
data.quote: To my dearest sister Stephanie, I am hoping this letter finds you in good health, which I am sadly unable to say I am currently in. I’ve had many bizarre dreams as of late, going from a lady to a butler serving my own family, to a mafia goon, to a mutant screeching they were a mathematician. I have been plagued by these dreams for weeks now. I’ve tried getting a doctor, but he seems to have misunderstood my conundrum. Best wishes, your spiffing sister D. Amsel.
data.firstNightReminder: Wake the Malady to show them the Grimoire, & prompt them to choose a player and an Outsider. Send the Malady to sleep. Wake the chosen player and a player of the Storyteller's choice (independently), show them the THIS CHARACTER SELECTED YOU info token, the Malady's token, and the chosen Outsider

data.name: Maligmaere
data.ability: If dead, you may (once) publicly guess the character of a good player who executed you or themselves. If correct, your team wins.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Maligmaere hunts down the good player who executed them.
howToRun: During the day, if the Maligmaere was executed by a good player, mark that good player with the HAUNTED token. If the Maligmaere was executed by an evil player, do not place the HAUNTED token.

During the day and whilst the HAUNTED token is placed, the Maligmaere may publicly claim to be the Maligmaere and guess the character of the player that executed them. Place the GUESS USED token on the Maligmaere, then allow them to say what it is. If incorrect, the Maligmaere may no longer guess. If correct, announce the game has ended and evil has won.
data.quote: Pareidoliac nightmares haunt your waking hours. Bodies hung amidst willow vines, veiled widows throw mirrors that release suffocating fog. You long for the day when your dreams foretell a time that cares, when your tears don't drown your pillow, when you don't scream at midnight so you don't hear that catastrophic bell ring in your head. Doom. Screech. The prophecy foretold your vague loss of self, where the portraits follow you around and your grandfather loses his teeth. Drop down now, heaven doesn't need you.

data.name: Siren
data.ability: A Townsfolk is poisoned. Once per game, at night*, choose that the Demon dies and you become the Demon.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Siren poisons a player, and can kill the Demon at night to give it a new lease on life.
howToRun: On the first night, place the Siren's 'Poisoned' token on any Townsfolk.

On nights other than the first, wake the Siren to use their ability: if no, put them back to sleep. If yes, remove the Siren's 'Poisoned' token, place the Siren's 'Dead' token on the Demon, and replace the Siren with the new Demon token. Place the global 'Starting Siren' token onto the new Demon, to indicate they used to be the Siren.
examples: Yesterday, the Undertow was executed and survived. Tonight, the Siren chooses to use their ability to kill the Undertow, and the Siren becomes the new Undertow. The Scuba Diver is no longer poisoned.
The Siren uses their ability whilst both Calamities live. Only one of them dies tonight.
tips: It's best to wait to use your ability. The longer you wait, the worse the poisoned Townsfolk gets and the better position you are in to become the Demon. However, if the Demon is in a tough spot, it's best to use your ability, likely publicly revealing the Siren began in play, so evil gains a fighting chance.
data.quote: The mistress of seduction - in a palace by the sea - drop a couple dragons - if you want time with me!
data.otherNightReminder: Wake the Siren and ask if they want to use their ability: if yes, make the Siren the demon and place the 'Dead' reminder token on the Demon.

data.name: Sister of Fey

data.quote: The court disproves of your babbling. I wish you to go mad dancing in a circle of mushrooms. Away!
data.firstNightReminder: Wake the Sister of Fey to learn which Townsfolk character was duplicated.
data.otherNightReminder: The 1sr time both of the duplicated Townsfolk are dead, all other good players are poisoned until tomorrow dusk.

data.lede: The Terror Brim haunts those they are closest to.
data.quote: Darkness manifests the grandest deerstalkers. The light manifests the deer.

data.quote: The universe is a grand pattern, beings of proportion and thought living in perfect order and paradigm. Crushed. Broken. Infested. You're all bugs with disgusting faces and bodies and repulsive gangly limbs. Slice. Bisect. The warp and weft. Divide. Conquer. It's almost done.

data.name: Canon Nade

data.creator: Pynstripe
data.quote: The wicked artillery set by thy father shall fire at midnight. Repent, make anew with thy father; there shan’t be freedom, nor tears of sympathy, nor have reverent willingness to bow, when those who have not bow’d in life shall be lowered to thy father’s eternal battlefield - where the cannonade shall be the final lullaby for sleepless nights.

data.name: Ephera
data.ability: Each night, choose a player (all learn who): they cannot be chosen or learned by abilities. After day 4, evil wins.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Ephera steals the essence of players.
summaryBullets: Each night, the Ephera chooses a player: all learn who. That player can no longer be chosen by abilities (including evil abilities), & cannot be learned in any form.
If a player attempts to choose or learn information about an Ephera chosen player, they are prompted to rechoose instead of losing their ability.
After day 4, evil wins.
examples: Zoey is the Ephera, who chooses Meg the Drunk. Meg is the only outsider, & now cannot be learned, so Carlos the Librarian learns there are no Outsiders in play.
That same day, Josephine the Artist asks the question “Is one of Zoey, Meg & Carlos the Demon?”. The Storyteller prompts her to ask a different question, as it cannot be information about Meg.
On night 2, Zoey chooses herself. Alfonse the Fearmonger chooses Zoey, & is prompted to rechoose.
data.quote: Surely by “capturing memories” you didn’t think you would be the one keeping them? How naïve mortals are…

summaryBullets: The evil Townsfolk keeps their regular ability, & may also wake for the Erosyon’s ability.
Only 1 of the Erosyon or the evil Townsfolk can wake to the Erosyon’s ability in a night. If the Townsfolk is dead, they can still wake for the Erosyon.

data.name: Maiden of Spikes
data.ability: Each night, choose 2 living players (not yourself). If neither were executed yesterday, choose 2 players tonight: they die.

On nights after the 1st, the Maiden of Spikes wakes to kill first. Then the 2 protected players are chosen.

The Maiden of Spikes may watch over any living players. If the Maiden of Spikes would choose to watch over any dead players, they are prompted to choose again. The Maiden of Spikes may not choose to watch over themself.

data.name: Mortdaine
data.ability: Each dusk, players pair up uniquely (if odd, 1 is alone): the 1st Townsfolk you pair with secretly becomes evil. After day 4, evil wins.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Mortdaine dances with players, turning them evil.
summaryBullets: At dusk, all players (including the dead & travellers) publicly declare another player they are pairing up with. All pairs must be agreed on by both, & all players must be paired. If there is an odd number of players, 1 player will be unpaired.
The 1st time a Townsfolk is paired up with the Mortdaine, they secretly become evil (even if dead or travellers). They are evil, & win or lose alongside evil.
Players must form unique pairs each dusk, changing who is with who. If there is an odd number of players, the solo player must also be unique.
If you’re playing in real life, players physically separate themselves into pairs.
After day 4, evil wins.
howToRun: On the 1st day, add the DAY 1 reminder to the Grimoire. On the 2nd day, add the DAY 2 reminder to the Grimoire. On the 3rd day, add the DAY 3 reminder to the Grimoire. On the 4th day, add the DAY 4 reminder to the Grimoire.

Each dusk, all players form unique pairs with players they haven't before. It is up to the players to remember who they have formed pairs with, & not repeat pairings. If there is an odd number of players, 1 will be alone & they may not be unpaired for more than 1 dusk.

The 1st time the Mortdaine is paired with a Townsfolk, place the Mortdaine's DANSE MACABRE reminder onto that Townsfolk. Tonight, that Townsfolk becomes evil & does not learn this happened, keeping the DANSE MACABRE reminder on the Townsfolk as a reminder of their new alignment.
examples: Felicity is the Mortdaine. The 1st Townsfolk she pairs up with is Margaret the Knight, who secretly becomes evil tonight. The 2nd is Liam the Town Crier, who remains good.

Hugo is the Mortdaine in a game with an odd number of players. He is left alone. Nobody becomes evil tonight, & everyone guffaws at Hugo for his social faux pas. From now on, Hugo must always pair up with a player.
data.quote: Shall we dance?
data.otherNightReminder: If a Townsfolk is marked with the Mortdaine's 'Danse Macabre' token, they become evil but does not wake to learn this.

data.name: Phlegm Fatale
data.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die; then you guess the most recent good executee’s character, & if correct, choose again.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Phlegm Fatale can gain additional kills if Town cannot obscure the characters of executed players.
summaryBullets: The Phlegm Fatale cannot gain more than 1 kill a night.
If no player has been executed, the Phlegm Fatale does not wake to choose an additional kill.
If an evil player is executed, the Phlegm Fatale still guesses the most recent good executee.
howToRun: Each day, if a good player is executed, mark them with the STAINED token. Do not mark evil players with this token at any point. If a good player is executed and a player already has the STAINED token, move it to the most recently executed good player, otherwise keep it on the original player.
Each night other than the first, wake the Phlegm Fatale to choose a player: they die, and are marked with the DEAD token. If no player has the STAINED token, put the Phlegm Fatale to sleep.

After killing, if a good player has the Phlegm Fatale's STAINED token, the Phlegm Fatale may guess their character. If incorrect, nothing happens and the Phlegm Fatale goes to sleep. If the Phlegm Fatale is correct, they may choose a player: they die, and are marked with a new DEAD token, and the Phlegm Fatale goes to sleep.
examples: The Erudite is executed. That night, the Phlegm Fatale is woken and kills the Electrician, and correctly guesses the Erudite's character, choosing to kill the Lounge Singer as their additional kill.
data.quote: If it's not Sanguine, I simply don't want it. You love me because I'm dangerous. data.name: Psaliphim
data.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. On the 2nd night, the Storyteller chooses who you & Minions are. [-? to +? Outsiders, no evil characters]
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Psaliphim converts good players into itself and Minions.
howToRun: During the setup of a Psaliphim game, do not add any evil characters into the bag. Replace them with good Townsfolk and Outsiders and send the bag out.
On the 1st night, do not run minion and demon info as there is no evil characters yet in play. Run everything else normally.
On the 2nd night, place COMMUNION tokens on each player who is turning into an evil Psaliphim or Minion. Wake these players, inform them of their new characters, alignment, and teammates.
On nights other than the first, wake the Psaliphim to choose a player, mark them with the Psaliphim's DEAD reminder.

On Night 2 and later Nights, wake the Psaliphim to choose a player: they die, place the 'Dead' token on them.

On day 4, all restrictions to speech are limited.

data.name: Undertow
data.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. The first time you are executed, you survive, and only you can die tonight.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Undertow survives the first time it is executed.
howToRun: During Setup, place the Undertow's 'Survives Execution' token on the Undertow.
During the day, if the Undertow is executed whilst it has it's 'Survives Execution' token, they survive execution. The 'Survives Execution' token is then removed.

Each night other than the first, wake the Undertow to choose a player: place the Undertow's 'Dead' token on that player. If the Undertow survived execution yesterday due to their own ability, do not place the 'Dead' token (unless it's on the Undertow themselves).
examples: On Day 3, the Undertow is executed for the first time and therefore doesn't die. The following night, no players (other than the Undertow) can die. Due to this, the Ruffian cannot cause an additional death due to their ability.
tips: The Undertow easily lends itself to bluff characters who can survive execution, but it has an easy tell. It might be best to sink (see the joke there?) kills after days when other players survive execution, to continually frame others as being the Undertow.

data.name: Xaoh
data.ability: Each night, something impossible occurs & you may silently suggest what to the Storyteller. Each night*, choose a player: they die.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Xaoh can cause impossible things to happen.
howToRun: If you wish to make setup impossible, make any changes before the bag goes out. Then, when the game begins, immediately place the 'Impoissibility' token on the Xaoh.

Each full day, from one dusk til the next, the Storyteller may break a single rule. If they do so, place the 'Impossibility' token on the most relevant player. The Storyteller may not break rules if the 'Impossibility' token is on the Grimoire, If there's an 'Impossibility' token on a player, remove it at dusk.
On future nights, The Xaoh points at any player. The chosen player dies—mark them with the "Dead" reminder token. Put the Xaoh to sleep
examples: The Sleepwalker was just killed by the Xaoh, but the Lounge Singer wakes up to learn the Nautilus' player. This is because Xaoh caused the Lounge Singer to become impossibly poisoned.
tips: The Xaoh's ability to break the game rules is quite vague, so the following are some uses of it: poisoning a player, waking up players when they shouldn't, redirecting the Xaoh's own kills to make them more effective, or announcing things that otherwise would not be possible.

data.name: Fascinated
data.ability: The Stoyteller has 1 vote each day, & declares its use before voting begins: something good might happen to players who also vote.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Fascinated provides the Storyteller a vote, & benefits those who vote with them.
summaryBullets: The Storyteller’s vote is like any other, and counts toward the vote total on the chosen player. They declare it publicly before all other players vote, starting the vote total at 1. They may only vote once per day.,
It is up to the Storyteller’s discretion who they vote for, and the Fascinated has no impact on who they vote for. The Storyteller may wish to help the Fascinated’s team with their public vote.

The Storyteller decides who benefits from voting alongside them. The Fascinated cannot inherently cause bad things to happen, but the positive effects on 1 team may weaken the other. The Storyteller should generally help the Fascinated’s team with ‘something good’. The Storyteller cannot lie about what ‘something good’ is.,
Something good may happen to the Fascinated if they vote alongside the Storyteller.,
Nothing happens due to the Fascinated’s ability on nominations where the Storyteller does not vote.
data.quote: Such a gorgeous melancholy. Laying down next to your grave. Your words, your majesty… your heart. I heard it like a posthumous songbird at my window, departed though time. Your Romantics have gone, their beauty lost to smog filled skies. But I know you. I know all about you. This garden is our Arcadia, your engraving my eclogue, thus I dance and sing around in glee like a child in a play. I shall talk to you forever, my lovely sweet departed poet. My myth.

data.name: Jetsetter
data.ability: Dead players don't use vote tokens on nominations you make. Players of your alignment you nominate might survive execution.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Jetsetter allows the dead to vote without using vote tokens, and may protect players of the same alignment they nominate
howToRun: If the Jetsetter nominates a player, run the nomination as normal. If the Jetsetter and the nominated player are the same alignment, you may place the Jetsetter's 'Survives Execution' token on that player.
If any dead players vote on the execution, do not remove their vote token. Instead, place the Jetsetter's 'Free Vote' token on them to indicate that they voted.
examples: The good Jetsetter nominates the Hush, and only they and the dead Industrialist vote on the execution. The Dead Industrialist doesn't lose their vote token. The Hush receives the correct amount of votes, and isn't replaced by another player. The Hush is then executed, and good wins.
tips: The Jetsetter can create a coalition of dead players, as they get to vote many more times per game than the limiting 1. Use it to your advantage, testing theories, or even protecting players you know to be the same alignment as you.

data.name: Mythos
data.ability: The 1st executed player grants an on-script ability to the Storyteller. The Storyteller's ability can be drunk or poisoned.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Mythos gives the 1st executed player a bond to the Storyteller.
summaryBullets: The 1st executed player chooses a Townsfolk, Outsider, Minion or Demon ability to give to the Storyteller. The Storyteller gains it, and uses it at it's appropriate place in the night order if it wakes.

If the chosen ability learns information, the executed player learns it, but does not make any associated choices. If an ability would not have any effect from the Storyteller gaining it, the Storyteller may prompt the executed player to choose again. If an ability is based off of positioning, it registers from the 1st executed player

The Storyteller, if they have an ability, can become a valid target for abilities that poison & drunk. The Storyteller's ability becoming drunk only applies to their ability, and does not make any other abilities malfunction. If the Storyteller has multiple abilities, only the one granted by the Mythos is affected.

When using the Mythos, the Storyteller needs to keep the game fair but also keep in the best interests of the executed player. A good player wants to solve the game, an evil player wishes to cover the truth - but if the executed player's team is winning / losing decidedly, it is ok to use the ability unoptimally / perfectly optimally to balance the teams.
examples: Dark, the Chef, is the first player executed this game. She grants the Storyteller the Fortune Teller’s ability. The Storyteller marks Procyon the Chambermaid as the Red Herring. The Storyteller chooses the BakedIce the Baron and Lady Mist the Saint, waking Dark to learn that neither are the Demon. The following night, the Storyteller chooses Procyon and Luis the Drunk, waking Dark to learn that either Procyon or Luis is the Demon.

Imze, the Cerenovus, is the first executed player executed this game. He grants the Storyteller the Goblin ability, but is denied as the Storyteller themself may not use it. They then grant the Storyteller the Poisoner’s ability.
data.quote: For a man who so despised the cold waves of the world, new passions were found in cosmic horrors. Naught more beautiful than the endless devouring mouths, seemingly coded to surpass the weak mortal mind. The folly of man, to expect that their ignorant species was more than a cog. It's well advised that you give power to these beings - before they're too far gone to even notice you.

data.name: Shapeshifter
data.ability: Each time a game ends, the script is modified & all players agree on how. The Storyteller may veto modifications.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Shapeshifter creates an ever-changing script.
summaryBullets: Modifications are based on group consensus, with the majority agreeing on which will be enacted.
There are no limit to the number of changes that can be made at once, but the Storyteller should limit the number to keep a consistent script identity.
The Storyteller may offer replacement ideas, but does not get a vote in which modifications should be made.
After each game, at least 1 modification must be made before the next game is run.
examples: The Storyteller presents a script called “Typhon’s Verona”, a teensyville centred around the Lord of Typhon. They declare they will veto attempts to add another demon or replace the Lord of Typhon. After the 1st game, the group agrees to replace the Goblin with the Marionette.

The group are undecided between replacing the Alchemist with the Slayer or Nightwatchman & cannot come to a consensus. The Storyteller breaks the tie, choosing to replace the Alchemist with the Slayer.
The group decides to make 4 modifications at once. The Storyteller decides to veto 3 of them.
data.quote: To dream is to die, to die is to be reborn, to be reborn is to become a rabbit, and to be a rabbit is a joy most mortals will never comprehend.

data.name: Thurifer
data.ability: At night, if 2 or less players would live, some deaths may be prevented so 3 players live at dawn, & all learn this occurred.
data.creator: Pynstripe
data.lede: The Thurifer makes high death scripts more reliable at lower player counts.
summaryBullets: On scripts where multiple characters can kill and especially at lower player counts, scenarios can occur when too many players die and the Storyteller has to force a team to win. The Thurifer can prevent this.
The Thurifer should not be used in scenarios where there is no player is executed when 3 players live.
The Storyteller decides which deaths are prevented due to the Thurifer's ability, to create the most fair scenario possible.
Players may not be revived due to the Thurifer's ability.
